data.hypothesis: A 256-source shared-memory tile should reduce redundant source loads across target threads, while factoring out the positive target mass and using rsqrtf should reduce interaction arithmetic. These are unmeasured hypotheses; the controller must check correctness and speed.
data.notes: Only baseline-e1 is a valid measured source and it passed all 11 listed correctness cases. The four research attempts ended in infrastructure errors without source or timing evidence. This candidate preserves the 28-byte Particle layout, mass output, one-kernel interface, and baseline 256/256/0 launch configuration. It has not been tested or independently confirmed.
transformations: Cooperatively stage each tile's source positions and masses in shared memory and reuse it across target threads, with barriers on every block path and safe tail handling.
Cancel the positive target-mass factor from the force and acceleration calculation; use rsqrtf to form the inverse-cube scale without changing compiler-wide math settings.
Retain self-interaction exclusion and skip exactly coincident displacement vectors; update velocity before position and leave the copied mass unchanged.
